title: Tech and Security Companies Respond to PHP2Shell Vulnerabilities
description: Two critical PHP vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, allow unauthenticated remote code execution. These bugs were discovered in August 2026 and patched by PHP on October 21, 2026, with updates for versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35. Exploitation attempts were detected before and after the patch release, including mass exploitation attempts shortly after fixes were published. Multiple vendors and governments have issued advisories urging immediate patching and thorough discovery of PHP installations, including those embedded in other software. Some organizations temporarily took affected sites offline to mitigate risk. Security firms have released detections and mitigations, and many vendors are reviewing their products for exposure. The vulnerabilities require precise conditions for exploitation but have been actively targeted in the wild.
aiSummary: The PHP2Shell vulnerabilities, identified as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, are critical remote code execution flaws affecting PHP. They allow unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code remotely. The vulnerabilities were discovered by Wiz, OpenAI, and Calif in August 2026 and publicly disclosed in October 2026. PHP released patches on October 21, 2026, for versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35. Exploitation attempts were observed prior to the embargo lift and continued after patches were released. Multiple security companies and governments have issued advisories and detection rules. Vendors including Cisco, Red Hat, Ubuntu, Debian, AWS, Google Cloud, cPanel, Plesk, and others have reviewed or patched their products. Some organizations have taken offline affected services as a precaution. The vulnerabilities require precise heap manipulation and timing for reliable exploitation, but unauthenticated remote code execution is possible under certain conditions. Detection and mitigation tools have been rapidly deployed by security firms.
aiImpact: Successful exploitation allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected PHP installations, potentially leading to full system compromise. Exploitation attempts have been observed in the wild, including mass exploitation shortly after patches were released. The vulnerabilities affect a wide range of PHP versions and, by extension, many commercial software products, appliances, and cloud services that embed PHP. This broad exposure increases the risk of compromise across diverse environments. Some vendors report that reliable exploitation requires non-default configurations or precise conditions, but unauthenticated code execution has been demonstrated in testing.
